text:
ara: Hey team — planning a small terraform change to tighten Karpenter scale-down grace periods and adjust HPA target utilization for tenant pools. Quick sanity check pls. TL;DR: reduce ttlSecondsAfterEmpty from 600 -> 300 for provisioner X, and change deployment hpa targetCPUUtilizationPercentage from 60 -> 55 for frontend-service.

lina: 👍 what's the motivation? production latency or cost?

ara: Mostly cost during low-traffic windows + quicker reclaim to free spot capacity. But worried about noisy evictions on bursty tenants.

mike: two quick checks — 1) are we using PDBs for stateful workloads in those nodegroups? 2) do we have evacuation probes for in-flight requests? If not, lowering TTL could surface 503s.

ara: Good call. We only have PDBs for DB pods; app pods rely on graceful termination. For probes, frontend has readiness/liveness but not a drain-safety annotation. Thinking to add `kubernetes.io/drain-delay: "30s"` style annotation to critical services.

sam: Can you paste the terraform snippet? I want to validate IAM and taints don't change.

ara: Sure — snippet below.

```hcl
resource "karpenter_provisioner" "tenant_pool_x" {
  name = "tenant-x"
  ttl_seconds_after_empty = 300
  labels = {
    workload = "tenant-x"
  }
  requirements = [
    { key = "karpenter.k8s.aws/instance-type", operator = "In", values = ["m6i.large"] }
  ]
}
```

lina: IAM looks unchanged. Any vault path/secret renames we need to sync? Last time a rename broke the metrics-adapter secret mount.

ara: Yeah I intend to rename `secret/data/tenant-x/provisioner` -> `secret/data/tenants/tenant-x/provisioner` as part of cleanup. Will update terraform mount. Reminder: metrics-adapter uses `vault.kv.path: tenants/` in a configmap.

mike: If you rename, we need a short migration: write new path then remove old after one rollover. Otherwise pods reading old path will crash on restart. Add a pre-deploy job that copies secrets in Vault.

ara: Good plan. I'll add a `null_resource` local-exec to run a `vault kv get` + `vault kv put` copy for migration.

jen: For the HPA tweak, do we have a canary roll? lowering target from 60 -> 55 reduces replicas in low traffic, might starve burst headroom.

ara: Plan is a canary on the tenant-x staging cluster: change HPA there, observe 48h, then roll to prod with rollout window 2h, revert policy in case of CPU spike.

infra-bot: [deploy-check] scanned 2100123456-karpenter-change: no conflicts, but flagged resource `frontend-deploy` for missing `drain-probe` annotation.

sam: infra-bot flagged the right thing. If we add drain-probe annotation, also ensure nginx/pod-disruption-tolerations are set.

ara: I'll add annotation + toleration snippet. Also will create a small chaostest to simulate scale-down during burst.

lina: Sounds good. Can you open a PR and tag `eng-infra` and `oncall`? If you want I can give a quick review.

ara: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/3425 — added terraform change, vault migration null_resource, and hpa canary job. @lina @mike please review when you get a sec.

mike: Reviewing now. If we can add a metric for queue-length to the HPA in addition to CPU that would help avoid premature scaling down.

ara: Noted — adding queue-backed metrics (keda) as fallback. I'll iterate in the PR.

jen: Thanks. If everything passes canary, schedule prod rollout during low-traffic window (Sat 02:00 UTC). I'll coordinate with oncall.

ara: Perfect. Will follow up in the PR with test results. :thumbsup:
